nodes.statement: \Cref{thm:cross-product-central}, \cref{lem:cross-product-basis} and \cref{cor:cross-product-simple}.

If $K/F$ is a finite dimensional and Galois field extension, the function $\mathfrak{C} : \mathrm{H}^{2}\left(\mathrm{Gal}(K/F), K^{\star}\right) \to \mathrm{Br}(K/F)$ defined by \[ \mathfrak{a} \mapsto \left[\mathfrak{C}_{\mathfrak{a}}\right]_{\sim_{\mathrm{Br}}} \] is well-defined.

nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak{a}$ and $\mathfrak{b}$ be two cohomologous 2-cocycles. By~\cref{def:second-group-coh}, for some $\mathfrak{c}: \mathrm{Gal}(K/F) \to K^{\star}$, for all $\sigma, \tau\in\mathrm{Gal}(K/F)$, we have \begin{equation} \frac{\sigma(\mathfrak{c}(\tau))}{\mathfrak{c}(\sigma\tau)}\mathfrak{c}(\sigma) = \frac{\mathfrak{a}(\sigma, \tau)}{\mathfrak{b}(\sigma, \tau)}. \end{equation} Let us denote $\mathsf{A}$ to be the $K$-basis $\{\Delta^{\mathfrak{a}}_{\sigma, 1} | \sigma\in\mathrm{Gal}(K/F)\}$ for $\mathfrak{C}_{\mathfrak{a}}$ and $\mathsf{B}$ to be the $K$-basis $\{\mathfrak{c}(\sigma)\cdot \Delta^{\mathfrak{b}}_{\sigma, 1}|\sigma\in\mathrm{Gal}(K/F)\}$ for $\mathfrak{C}_{\mathfrak{b}}$. We immediately have a $K$-linear isomorphism $\phi : \mathfrak{C}_{\mathfrak{a}}\cong \mathfrak{C}_{\mathfrak{b}}$ by mapping $\mathsf{A}$ to $\mathsf{B}$. Since the $K$-action on $\mathfrak{C}_{a}$ and $\mathfrak{C}_{b}$ agrees with the $F$-action on them (\cref{con:cross-product-iota}), $\phi$ is also an $F$-linear isomorphism. By~\cref{con:compare-conj-factors}, we have that $\iota_{\mathfrak{C}_{\mathfrak{a}}}\left(\mathrm{comp}^{x}_{\Delta_{\sigma, 1}, \Delta_{\tau, 1}, \Delta_{\sigma\tau, 1}}\right) = \Delta_{\sigma, 1}\Delta_{\tau, 1}\Delta_{\sigma\tau, 1}^{-1} = \mathfrak{a}(\sigma,\tau)\cdot \Delta_{\sigma\tau, 1}\Delta_{\sigma\tau, 1}^{-1} = \mathfrak{a}(\sigma,\tau)\cdot 1 = \Delta_{\mathsf{id},\mathfrak{a}(\sigma,\tau)}$ which is precisely $\iota_{\mathfrak{C}_{\mathfrak{a}}}(\mathfrak{a}(\sigma,\tau))$.

nodes.statement: Let $X \in \mathrm{Br}(K/F)$, $A$ be an arbitrary good representation of $X$ and $x$ be an arbitrary $A$-conjugation sequence which exists by~\cref{cor:mem-relative-br-iff-good-rep} and~\cref{con:exists-conj-seq}. By~\cref{def:good-rep}, $X = \left[A\right]_{\sim_{\mathrm{Br}}}$. Hence by~\cref{cor:to-2-cocylce-wd} and~\cref{thm:snd-coh-to-relative-br}, we evaluate the composition at $X$ as: \begin{center} \begin{tikzcd} {[A]_{\sim_{\mathrm{Br}}}} \arrow[mapsto]{r} & {\left[\mathcal{B}^2_x\right]} \arrow[mapsto]{r} & {\left[\mathfrak{C}_{\mathcal{B}^2_x}\right]} \end{tikzcd}. \end{center} Hence we need to prove that $A$ and $\mathfrak{C}_{\mathcal{B}^{2}_{x}}$ are Brauer equivalent. We will show that they are isomorphic as $F$-algebras. since $\{x_{\sigma}|\sigma\in\mathrm{Gal}(K/F)\}$ is a $K$-basis for $A$ and $\{\Delta_{\sigma, 1}|\sigma \in \mathrm{Gal}(K/F)\}$ is a $K$-basis for $\mathfrak{C}_{\mathcal{B}^{2}_{x}}$, they are certainly isomorphic as $K$-modules. Let $\phi : \mathfrak{C}_{\mathcal{B}^{2}_{x}} \cong A$ be the $K$-linear isomorphism defined by $\Delta_{\sigma, 1} \mapsto x_{\sigma}$, since the $K$-action on $A$ and the $F$-action on $A$ are compatible (\cref{con:good-rep-mod}), $\phi$ is also an $F$-linear isomorphism. Like in~\cref{thm:snd-coh-to-relative-br}, we check that $\phi(1) = 1$ and $\phi(xy)=\phi(x)\phi(y)$ for all $x,y \in A$: \begin{enumerate} \item preservation of one: by~\cref{con:compare-conj-factors}, we have \[ \begin{aligned} \phi(1) &= \phi\left(\Delta_{\mathsf{id},\mathcal{B}^{2}_{x}(\mathsf{id},\mathsf{id})^{-1}}\right) \\ &= \mathcal{B}^{2}_{x}(\mathsf{id},\mathsf{id})^{-1} \phi\left(\Delta_{\mathsf{id}, 1}\right) \\ &= \mathcal{B}^{2}_{x}(\mathsf{id},\mathsf{id})^{-1} x_{\mathsf{id}} \\ &= \mathrm{comp}_{x_{\mathsf{id}},x_{\mathsf{id}},x_{\mathsf{id}}}^{-1} x_{\mathsf{id}} \\ &= \mathrm{comp}_{x_{\mathsf{id}},x_{\mathsf{id}},x_{\mathsf{id}}} x_{\mathsf{id}} x_{\mathsf{id}} x_{\mathsf{id}}^{-1} \\ &= x_{\mathsf{id}} x_{\mathsf{id}}^{-1} \\ &= 1. \end{aligned} \] \item preservation of multiplication: let $\sigma,\tau\in\mathrm{Gal}(K/F)$ and $c,d \in K$, by~\cref{con:compare-conj-factors} and~\cref{def:conj-factor}, we have \[ \begin{aligned} \phi\left(\Delta_{\sigma,c}\Delta_{\tau,d}\right) &= \phi\left(\Delta_{\sigma\tau, c\sigma(d)\mathcal{B}^{2}_{x}(\sigma,\tau)}\right) \\ &= c\sigma(d)\mathcal{B}^{2}_{x}(\sigma,\tau) \,\cdot\, \phi\left(\Delta_{\sigma\tau, 1}\right) \\ &= c\sigma(d)\mathcal{B}^{2}_{x}(\sigma,\tau) \,\cdot\, x_{\sigma\tau} \\ &= c\sigma(d)\mathrm{comp}_{x_{\sigma},x_{\tau},x_{\sigma\tau}} \,\cdot\, x_{\sigma\tau} \\ &= c\sigma(d)\,\cdot\, \iota_{A}\left(\mathrm{comp}_{x_{\sigma},x_{\tau},x_{\sigma\tau}}\right)x_{\sigma\tau} \\ &= c\sigma(d) \,\cdot\, x_{\sigma}x_{\tau}\\ \phi\left(\Delta_{\sigma,c}\right)\phi\left(\Delta_{\tau,d}\right) &=\left(c \cdot \phi\left(\Delta_{\sigma, 1}\right)\right) \left(d \cdot \phi\left(\Delta_{\tau, 1}\right)\right) \\ &= \left(c \cdot x_{\sigma}\right) \left(d \cdot x_{\tau}\right)\\ &= c \,\cdot\, x_{\sigma}\iota_{A}(d) x_{\tau} \\ &= c\sigma_{d} \,\cdot\, x_{\sigma}x_{\tau}. \end{aligned} \] \end{enumerate}

In fact, $\phi$ is also an $F$-algebra homomorphism: \begin{enumerate} \item $\phi(1) = 1$: indeed $\phi\left(\Delta_{\mathsf{id},1}\right) = \mathsf{id}$. \item $\phi(xy) = \phi(x)\phi(y)$: indeed, let $\sigma,\tau\in\mathrm{Gal}(K/F)$ and $c,d\in K$, we need to check that $\phi\left(\Delta_{\sigma,c}\Delta_{\tau,d}\right) = \phi\left(\Delta_{\sigma,c}\right)\phi\left(\Delta_{\tau,d}\right)$. The left hand side is equal to \[\phi\left(\Delta_{\sigma\tau,c\sigma(d)}\right) = \phi\left(c\sigma(d)\,\cdot\, \Delta_{\sigma\tau,1}\right) = c\sigma(d)\,\cdot\, \sigma\tau;\] and the right hand side is equal to \[ \phi\left(c\cdot \Delta_{\sigma,1}\right)\phi\left(d\cdot \Delta_{\tau, 1}\right) = (c \cdot \sigma) (d \cdot \tau). \] For any $x \in K$, applying left hand side to $x$ will result in $c\sigma(d)\sigma(\tau(x))$ while right hand side will result in $c\sigma(d\tau(x))$, hence both sides are equal. \end{enumerate} Hence, $\phi$ is an $F$-algebra isomorphism by~\cref{cor:alghom-bijective-of-dim-eq}; that is we have $\mathfrak{C}_{1} \cong \mathrm{End}_{F}K \cong\mathrm{Mat}_{\dim_{F}K}(F)$.
